key_insight: A hybrid quantum-classical MCMC sampler can generate realistic Lagrangian tracer dispersion statistics in turbulent shear flows by using a quantum circuit to propose correlated acceleration samples.
engineering_relevance: This suggests a potential quantum generative module for turbulence and transport simulation, especially where multivariate cross-correlations make classical sampling harder.
method: Parametric quantum circuit builds the proposal distribution for Metropolis-Hastings.
Samples turbulent acceleration vectors in a joint distribution over all 3 components plus height.
Uses a tempered target distribution and compares against classical MCMC and Langevin transport models.
evidence_signal: The generated tracer-pair dispersion scaling laws agree with the stochastic Langevin model and classical MCMC, and the height-weighted spectral gap is larger than classical MCMC at the highest qubit/resolution settings.
watch_item: The method is only demonstrated reliably at relatively small scale (Nq <= 6 per spatial dimension), so scalability and hardware noise remain key concerns.
paper_title: Quantum-enhanced Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling to model Lagrangian tracer dispersion in turbulent boundary layer
